notes_list.title: Cannizzaro Reaction
notes_list.basic_overview: Non-enolizable aldehydes can disproportionate in concentrated base to an alcohol and a carboxylate.
notes_list.extra_info_content: One aldehyde molecule is oxidized while another is reduced. Crossed Cannizzaro often uses formaldehyde as the species oxidized to formate.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Concentrated aqueous base; non-enolizable aldehydes are required for the classic reaction.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: OH− addition to aldehyde → tetrahedral intermediate → hydride transfer to a second aldehyde molecule → alcohol + carboxylate.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: The key hydride-transfer step couples oxidation and reduction. Product distribution depends on substrate and base concentration.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Distinguish from aldol by checking α-H.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not apply Cannizzaro to ordinary enolizable aldehydes where aldol chemistry is available under suitable conditions.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
